Read a class Tonel source (input: class name).
chatParticipant.pharo.command.listPackag: List packages available in the image.
chatParticipant.pharo.command.listClasse: List classes of a package (input: package name).
chatParticipant.pharo.command.eval.descr: Evaluate Smalltalk and return the result (confirmation required).
chatParticipant.pharo.command.runClassTe: Run all tests of a class.

lmTool.createPackage.modelDescription: Creates a package in the Pharo image (has side effects).
lmTool.createPackage.userDescription: Create a package in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.createClass.modelDescription: Creates a class (Tonel) in a package in the Pharo image (has side effects).
lmTool.createClass.userDescription: Create a class in a package in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.readClass.modelDescription: Reads the Tonel source of a class from the Pharo image (no side effects).
lmTool.readClass.userDescription: Read the source of a class from the active Pharo image.
lmTool.listPackages.modelDescription: Lists packages present in the Pharo image (no side effects).
lmTool.listPackages.userDescription: List packages available in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.listClasses.modelDescription: Lists classes of a package in the Pharo image (no side effects).
lmTool.listClasses.userDescription: List classes of a package in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.eval.modelDescription: Executes Smalltalk code in the Pharo image and returns the result (may have side effects).
lmTool.eval.userDescription: Execute Smalltalk code in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.runClassTests.modelDescription: Runs all tests of a class in the Pharo image.
lmTool.runClassTests.userDescription: Run all tests for a class in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.runTestMethod.modelDescription: Runs a test method (class + selector) in the Pharo image.
lmTool.runTestMethod.userDescription: Run one test method in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.iceListChanges.modelDescription: Lists server-reported image-vs-repository changes, Iceberg index changes, and dirty VS Code buffers. Reads in-memory state — no extra LSP call. Returns changes, stagedChanges, and unsavedBuffers (URIs) per repository. Unsaved buffers have not yet been saved to the active image.
lmTool.iceListChanges.userDescription: List image, Iceberg index, and unsaved editor-buffer changes by repository.
lmTool.iceListChanges.input.repositoryNa: Name of the Iceberg repository to inspect. If omitted, all valid repositories are listed.
lmTool.iceShowDiff.modelDescription: Returns the unified diff of a resource tracked by Iceberg and optionally opens the diff editor. The original content is fetched via the existing pharoImage FileSystem provider (no extra LSP call). Call pharo-ice-list-changes first to get a URI.
lmTool.iceShowDiff.userDescription: Show the Iceberg diff for a resource in the active Pharo image.
lmTool.iceShowDiff.input.uri.description: URI of the changed resource (e.g. pharoImage:/MyPackage/MyClass.class.st).
Repository name used in the diff editor title (optional).
lmTool.iceShowDiff.input.openEditor.desc: Open the VS Code diff editor in addition to returning the patch text (default: true).
configuration.pharo.pathToVM.description: The Pharo VM used to run the Pharo image hosting the Pharo Language Server. Set an executable path or a command available on PATH (for example, pharo). Choose a VM compatible with the selected image.
configuration.pharo.pathToImage.descript: The Pharo image that can run the Pharo Language Server (https://github.com/badetitou/Pharo-LanguageServer).
configuration.pharo.imageWorkspace.descr: Expose pharoImage:/ as a workspace folder so extensions supporting virtual workspaces (for example AI assistants) can read classes from the running image.
configuration.pharo.headless.description: Whether the Pharo image should run in headless mode.
configuration.pharo.debugMode.descriptio: Run the image in debug mode (cannot be used in headless mode).
configuration.pharo.quickInstall.imageNa: The image to download by default when using the install command.
configuration.pharo.quickInstall.serverV: The server version to install by default.
The VM version required by default for the selected server.
